title: Coherence measurement interchange, version 1
description: Structural counts produced by some tool, in a shape this ratchet can hold a line on. The reference extractor reads Python; the judgement is language-neutral, and this schema is what lets the two come apart. Two properties are load-bearing. Counts are raw, never ratios or composite scores: a score falls when the codebase grows while the raw counts hold, so a score cannot be ratcheted honestly. And every count is a candidate, never an observation: this tool did not read that code, so the producer travels with the numbers and a person still decides what any of it means.

produced_by.description: Which tool made these counts, at which version, against which of its own schema versions. A grounding pack built on imported facts names this, so a reader can tell which parser produced them.

producer_schema.description: The producer's own schema version this adapter was written against. An adapter meeting a version it has not been read against refuses rather than guessing.

source.description: What was measured and when, in the producer's own terms.

epistemic.description: Imported counts are always candidates. There is deliberately no way to declare them observed: only the extractor that read the code may claim that, and only a named person may ratify anything on their strength.

counts.description: Signal name to raw count. Names are namespaced by producer (`drift.architecture_violation`) so an imported signal cannot be confused with one this tool measured. Every signal the producer reported is carried; dropping the unrecognised ones would baseline a narrower portfolio than the reader believes they set.

raw.description: A count, not a ratio and not a score. This field is the whole reason the schema exists.

sites.description: Where the producer found each thing it counted, so a count can be read back to a file and a line rather than taken on faith.
